title: Last Bell, 2008
logline: The bell. Wood is at the laundromat, restocking a rack that's been empty of digests for five years. Old habit. He hears it from there.

panels.composition: The laundromat. WOOD at the free rack, not restocking anything — there's nothing to restock — just straightening the real-estate flyers. BARNABY. The OWNER, older, folding.

balloons.text: Come in and touch the rack.

image.prompt: a thin man straightening real-estate flyers in a laundromat's free rack with a dog beside him, an older man folding towels, muddy flats

panels.composition: The bell, through the window, jagged. 3:05.

image.prompt: a laundromat window with a jagged bell-sound shape drawn coming through it

panels.composition: Wood's hand on the empty slot in the rack where the digest went.

image.prompt: close-up of a hand resting on an empty slot in a wire free-paper rack, no words

panels.composition: Wood and the dog leaving. The owner watching. The rack, with everything in it but the thing he touched.

image.prompt: a thin man and a dog leaving a laundromat past a free rack, an older man watching them go, no words

art.line: brush-pen; the flats cleaner; Sundays the point

notes: Five years since the digest. He still touches the rack.
